tagline: Up Mount Prospect to John Weeks's stone tower.
intro: Off US 3 just south of Lancaster, a narrow auto road, counted among the first scenic byways in the state, climbs Mount Prospect through the woods. Pullouts along the way look out on the Connecticut River and the White Mountains. At the top stands the summer estate of John Wingate Weeks, a stucco house under a red tile roof, with its carriage house and a round stone tower.

Weeks grew up in Lancaster and, as a congressman, carried the Weeks Act of 1911, which let the government buy land for national forests in the East. The White Mountain National Forest it made possible is in view from the summit.

moments.title: Stone observation tower
moments.text: From the round stone tower, built around a water tank, the view runs all the way around, to the Presidential Range, the Green Mountains of Vermont, the Kilkenny Range and the Percy Peaks.

moments.title: Weeks house
moments.text: Weeks died here at his summer home, and the house museum tells of the family and of his part in the early conservation movement.
